title: Top scorer per subject
prompt: Return the student, subject, and score for whoever scored the highest in each subject (ties should both appear). Do not use RANK, ROW_NUMBER, or any window function — instead use a correlated subquery: a row qualifies if a COUNT of same-subject rows with a strictly higher score equals zero.
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE score18 (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, student TEXT, subject TEXT, score REAL); INSERT INTO score18 VALUES (1,'Amy','Math',88),(2,'Ben','Math',95),(3,'Cara','Math',70),(4,'Dan','Science',80),(5,'Ella','Science',92),(6,'Finn','Science',92);
reference_sql: SELECT student, subject, score FROM score18 s1 WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM score18 s2 WHERE s2.subject = s1.subject AND s2.score > s1.score) = 0;
